title: OS.get_cmdline_args() does not contain OS.get_cmdline_user_args()
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in Godot 4.5.0
-  I intend to test mast and test some older builds.

### System information

Godot v4.5.stable (876b29033) - Linux Mint 22.2 (Zara) on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Ti (nvidia; 580.95.05) - AMD Ryzen 9 3900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 62.71 GiB memory

### Issue description

Per the documentation we are lead to believe that OS.get_cmdline_args() returns all command line args to include user args. It is already known in other issues that Godot is hiding certain command line args which are specific to Godot, so I am not addressing that here.
Excerpt [From the Docs for stable 4.5](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_os.html#class-os-method-get-cmdline-user-args)
```gdscript
# Godot has been executed with the following command:
# godot --fullscreen -- --level=2 --hardcore

OS.get_cmdline_args()      # Returns ["--fullscreen", "--level=2", "--hardcore"]
OS.get_cmdline_user_args() # Returns ["--level=2", "--hardcore"]
```

### Steps to reproduce

However the reality is this:
```gdscript
# Godot has been executed with the following command:
# godot --fullscreen -- --level=2 --hardcore

OS.get_cmdline_args()      # Returns an empty array as [] because Godot has swallowed the --fullscreen argument.
OS.get_cmdline_user_args() # Returns ["--level=2", "--hardcore"]
```
Godot is actually parsing the command line arguments and then separating them into 2 separate arrays, normal command line arguments and user command line arguments.
This behavior is in many ways useful. But since it conflicts with documentation it is very confusing and unexpected.

Note: I changed the command line argument from --fullscreen to instead be --some_command_line_arg because based on what I was reading in the other similar issues --fullscreen might actually be problematic as it may be swallowed by Godot.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)
I had to include the .godot folder in order to preserve the multiple debug instances.
[os.get-cmdline-args-vs-os.get-cmdline-user-args_30DEC2025.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24388948/os.get-cmdline-args-vs-os.get-cmdline-user-args_30DEC2025.zip)
If you run this MRP it should run 2 instances.
The first instance has the following command line arguments: --some_cmd_line_arg -- --some_user_arg --level=2  and it prints: 
```
["--scene", "uid://daxdq3ddnnqpp", "--some_cmd_line_arg"]
   At: res://mrp.gd:5:_ready()
["--some_user_arg", "--level=2"]
   At: res://mrp.gd:6:_ready()
```
The second instance has the following command line arguments: --fullscreen --headless --some_cmd_line_arg -- --some_user_arg --level=2 
and it prints:
```
["--scene", "uid://daxdq3ddnnqpp", "--some_cmd_line_arg"]
   At: res://mrp.gd:5:_ready()
["--some_user_arg", "--level=2"]
   At: res://mrp.gd:6:_ready()
```
This further proves my point about the documentation being wrong and misleading as you can see the --fullscreen is indeed swallowed by Godot.

No Longer Relevant: ~~I will make an MRP soon. I may need to keep the .godot file if I am going to reproduce the command line issues using the multiple instance running in Godot, but we will see soon enough in the future.~~
